subject: general
question: Which of the following administrative features was common to both Pallava and Pandya kingdoms?

options.text: Division of the kingdom into Mandalams and Nadus
Village assemblies were called Sabha and Ur

solution:
The correct answer is __**Village assemblies were called Sabha and Ur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pallava** and **Pandya kingdoms** were prominent dynasties in South India known for their administrative systems and unique governance. One of the common administrative features between them was the existence of **village assemblies**, termed as **Sabha** and **Ur**.
 
• **Village Assemblies:** Sabha and Ur were local self-governing bodies that managed village affairs, including resource distribution, judicial administration, and revenue collection. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Sabha:** Sabha referred to an assembly of Brahmin villages (agraharas) and was responsible for handling religious and administrative matters in the village. This assembly was highly structured and worked based on committees. *Hence, this was common in both kingdoms.*
 
• **Ur:** Ur was the assembly of non-Brahmin villages, which handled administrative functions like managing agricultural lands, water resources, and solving disputes among villagers. This was also common to Pallava and Pandya kingdoms. *Hence, this is correct.*
 
• The existence of these village assemblies shows the decentralized governance system of both kingdoms, wherein local communities had significant autonomy in decision-making. *Thus, this was a shared feature between the Pallava and Pandya kingdoms.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallava Kingdom:**

 
 
• **Time Period:** The Pallavas ruled from the **3rd century CE to the 9th century CE**. They were primarily centered in the region of present-day Tamil Nadu.
 
• **Achievements:** The Pallavas were known for their **architectural advancements**, including the rock-cut temples of Mahabalipuram and the Kailasanatha temple in Kanchipuram.
 
• **Administrative System:** Their governance was characterized by strong central authority, yet local administration was effectively managed by village assemblies like Sabha and Ur.
 
 
 
• **Pandya Kingdom:**
 
 
• **Time Period:** The Pandyas ruled from the **6th century BCE to the 16th century CE**. Their kingdom was located in the southern part of Tamil Nadu.
 
• **Achievements:** The Pandyas were known for their **literature, art, and trade relations** with countries like Rome and Southeast Asia.
 
• **Administrative System:** Similar to the Pallavas, the Pandyas also relied on village assemblies like Sabha and Ur for local governance. This decentralized system ensured efficient management of resources.
 
 
 
• **Village Assemblies:**
 
 
• The village assemblies played a significant role in ensuring that the administration of villages was carried out effectively. They were involved in matters like taxation, revenue collection, irrigation management, and resolving disputes.
 
• **Sabha and Ur:** These assemblies were the backbone of local governance during the Pallava and Pandya periods. They were highly structured and functioned through committees dedicated to specific tasks.
